# Founding Fuel — Innovation & R&D: Batch 1 (2015) — Dense Observations

---

## RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES ON THIS THEME

**Innovation requires systemic conditions, not just individual genius**
- "Innovation has to move from being the province of a few to a more widely spread activity" — SOURCE: "Why you need to have a chief innovation officer" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-06-01)
- The Tata Innovista example (2,700+ teams, 65 companies, 18 countries, 30,000 participants over a decade) is held up as proof that sustained institutional scaffolding — not one-off programs — creates innovation culture — SOURCE: "Lessons from the House of Tata on Technology and Innovation" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-05-04)
- Linda Hill's "collective genius" argument demolishes the "solo genius" myth: "innovation is a collaborative effort, featuring many individuals' contributions, several missteps, false starts and combinations of several ideas" — SOURCE: "Everybody Has a Slice of Genius" by CKGSB Knowledge (2015-07-11)

**Business model innovation > product innovation**
- "The most successful innovations share two traits: They focus on shifts in the business model and customer experience. They employ multiple kinds of innovation—frequently six or more" — SOURCE: "How to build a business model" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-24)
- Erik Roth (McKinsey): "Technologies do not disrupt, business models disrupt." 85% of CEOs say innovation is top of agenda; 80% say their business models are at risk; only 6% say they have the capability required to survive — SOURCE: "Technologies do not disrupt, business models disrupt" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-10-26)
- "In the future, success will be determined not as much by strategy, but by how innovative a business model is" — SOURCE: "How to build a business model" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-24)

**Self-disruption as survival strategy**
- "You have to become your own fiercest competitor and disrupt or destroy your own business before competition does" — SOURCE: "Disrupt or destroy your own business to make it stronger" by Founding Fuel (2015-06-01)
- Amazon's Lab126/Kindle, Netflix's streaming pivot, Haier's micro-enterprise transformation all cited as models — SOURCE: "Disrupt or destroy your own business to make it stronger" (2015-06-01); "Haier is disrupting itself" by CKGSB Knowledge (2015-10-16); "Haier CEO Zhang Ruimin" by CKGSB Knowledge (2015-10-18)
- Harsh Mariwala explicitly applies this to Marico: "I knew it wouldn't be easy and I would inevitably have to look outside for help... Even now, as an organization, we never shy away from listening to people who challenge our world-view. Else we fear we will atrophy" — SOURCE: "It's time to destroy your business" by Harsh Mariwala (2015-08-31)

**Framing the right question is the genesis of innovation**
- "All discovery, all invention, all innovation are outcomes of curiosity, of inquisitiveness, of asking all manner of questions" — SOURCE: "Why questions score over answers" by Founding Fuel (2015-06-26)
- Dell's origin story: Michael Dell asked "Why should a computer cost 5x the sum of its parts?" — a question that generated an entire business model — SOURCE: "Are you asking the right question?" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-29)
- Low-cost carriers converting costs to revenue by reframing questions — SOURCE: "Are you asking the right question?" (2015-04-29); "How to turn problems into solutions" (2015-04-29)

**Design thinking as a systematic innovation discipline**
- "Design thinking is actually a systematic approach to problem solving that starts with customers and has the ability to create a better future for them" — SOURCE: "The Power of Design" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-13)
- "Designers train themselves to unlearn. They reimagine and rethink." — SOURCE: "What start-ups ought to do now" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-25)
- The Jeevan Bindi (iodine patch as bindi for rural women) is FF's go-to example of design thinking transforming lives at scale — SOURCE: "The Power of Design" (2015-04-13)
- Design thinking workshop forces recognition that gut instinct without structured tools produces only 2-3 ideas vs. many more with methodology — SOURCE: "The nonsense that is gut instinct" by Charles Assisi (2015-12-14)

**Growth hacking as the replacement for traditional marketing**
- "Traditional marketing can also be called interruption marketing—'hey, stop what you are doing and let me convince you to buy something you likely don't need'" — SOURCE: "Traditional marketing is dead" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-06)
- Dropbox's referral loop, Google's free-then-monetize-users model, Gmail's artificial scarcity — all cited as canonical growth hacking — SOURCE: "Traditional marketing is dead" (2015-04-06); "Develop a Growth Hacker's mindset" (2015-05-13)
- Sean Ellis's definition: "whose true north is growth. Everything they do is scrutinized by its potential impact on scalable growth" — SOURCE: "Develop a Growth Hacker's mindset" (2015-05-13)

**Agility ≠ adaptability; strategic agility requires integrating short-term and long-term**
- "Adaptability is about slow change, while agility is about quick response" — SOURCE: "7 Lessons About Agility" by Baba Prasad (2015-06-27)
- The "Bear and Hikers Paradigm" (sacrifice a friend to outrun the bear = expedient but shortsighted) vs. the "Broken Cup Paradigm" (handling failure as a moment of learning with long-term impact) — SOURCE: "Enabling Strategic Agility in Organizations" by Baba Prasad (2015-08-11)
- "In a truly agile company, strategy, innovation, and leadership are integrated" — SOURCE: "7 Lessons About Agility" (2015-06-27)

---

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**The foundational question FF returns to obsessively**: Why has India not produced radical/breakthrough technological innovation despite having world-class talent?

- Narayana Murthy's question: "Why has there been no earth-shaking invention or technology from India over the last 60 years?" — and FF takes the question seriously rather than defensively — SOURCE: "Indian Innovation: Too much Valley Kool-Aid without the Valley" by Baba Prasad (2015-08-15)
- Rishikesha Krishnan frames it as: "Indian companies have stayed quite some distance away from radical technological innovation" — SOURCE: "Tech-savvy entrepreneurs, can you put India on the global innovation map?" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-12-21)
- The book *From Jugaad to Systematic Innovation: The Challenge for India* (Krishnan) is cited as the systemic-level analysis — SOURCE: "Lessons from Vertex Pharma" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-03-16)

**India's VC ecosystem problem**: FF is skeptical of the Indian VC community's cookie-cutter approach
- "It uses a cookie cutter approach with very limited imagination. They would rather blow their cash on an app (without proof of concept) than on a good service model that has growth potential. We pretend in India to be like the Silicon Valley guys, but we don't really have the b****s!" — SOURCE: "Getting The Funding Piece Right" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-09-08)
- Most Indian VCs "act like bankers. They give you an umbrella when the sun is shining, and take it away when it rains" — SOURCE: "Don't comment on the library. Read the books" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-19)
- The herd mentality is named: "apps are the new sunshine" — SOURCE: "Getting The Funding Piece Right" (2015-09-08)
- Israel's Yozma model (fund of funds, tech investors with operating experience) held up as the model India should follow — SOURCE: "Getting The Funding Piece Right" (2015-09-08)

**India-specific innovation examples FF celebrates**:
- Team Indus (Google Lunar XPRIZE) — "audacious spunk," multi-disciplinary, no aerospace background — SOURCE: "It's Not Just Rocket Science Dummy!" by N S Ramnath (2015-04-20)
- InMobi's Miip launch: described as "virtuoso performance that had a clear Steve Jobs touch" — "the really momentous news of the coming of age of a serious desi challenger got lost in the noise" — SOURCE: "InMobi's Miip May Be More Important to India than Pichai" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-08-26)
- FreeCharge: celebrated for having 14,000 transactions/day with zero marketing spend at founding — SOURCE: "How FreeCharge found its Mojo" by Shailendra Singh (2015-04-13)
- Aravind Eye Hospitals, Jeevan Bindi, Multix vehicle, GE Healthcare India's ground-up BoP products — SOURCE: "How to build a business model" (2015-03-24); "The Power of Design" (2015-04-13); "Revisiting innovation at the bottom of the pyramid" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-12-01)

**Bottom of the pyramid as India's distinctive innovation mandate**:
- GE Healthcare India: started with how rural India actually keeps premature babies warm (200-watt bulb), built ground-up — SOURCE: "Revisiting innovation at the bottom of the pyramid" (2015-12-01)
- Kashyap's formula: "75% of the functionality at 50% of the cost" — though Rajan (GE) suggests even more extreme affordability required (CT scan: $584 US vs. $43 India) — SOURCE: "Revisiting innovation at the bottom of the pyramid" (2015-12-01)
- Polaris-Eicher Multix: "designed for transporting goods, buying supplies, taking the family on an outing or even providing a power back-up for a small home" — SOURCE: "Revisiting innovation at the bottom of the pyramid" (2015-12-01)

**India's regulatory environment as innovation obstacle**:
- "India doesn't have an entrepreneur-friendly culture. Regulations are overwhelming. The government's answer to people breaking the laws is writing more laws, not enforcing them." — SOURCE: "Don't comment on the library. Read the books" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-19)
- Druva's Jaspreet Singh moved to Silicon Valley because he thought he couldn't build a global product company from India — SOURCE: "Don't comment on the library. Read the books" (2015-03-19)

**R&D tax breaks: FF publishes a skeptical deconstruction**:
- Sachin Joneja argues R&D tax breaks reward wrong behavior at the wrong time, don't actually drive R&D location decisions, and that Xerox PARC is the world's "most famous vanity project" — SOURCE: "Is the R&D tax break really an incentive to innovate?" by Sachin Joneja (2015-11-26); "If not tax breaks to seed innovation, then what?" by Sachin Joneja (2015-12-05)
- The real driver of R&D: competitive intensity in the marketplace — "The only thing that can work is to increase the competitive intensity of the marketplace" — SOURCE: "If not tax breaks to seed innovation, then what?" (2015-12-05)

**The "Valley Kool-Aid" critique — distinctive and pointed**:
- Baba Prasad: "the flow of ideas is one-directional. Ideas from the West are absorbed and spouted in India as if they were divine truth, but there is absolutely [no return flow]" — SOURCE: "Indian Innovation: Too much Valley Kool-Aid without the Valley" (2015-08-15)
- The father-in-law story: Harvard PhD in English, returned to Poona University in 1961 because "there was magic in the air in India then" — and that magic is now gone — SOURCE: "Indian Innovation: Too much Valley Kool-Aid without the Valley" (2015-08-15)

**India's technology sourcing vulnerability**:
- Large Indian company (unnamed) that sourced technology from global leaders now finds those companies are its largest competitors and won't license anymore — SOURCE: "Tech-savvy entrepreneurs, can you put India on the global innovation map?" (2015-12-21)
- "India's stand at the Paris Climate Change talks shows that our failure to develop 'clean' technologies is clearly preventing us from taking on more aggressive emission control targets" — SOURCE: "Tech-savvy entrepreneurs, can you put India on the global innovation map?" (2015-12-21)

**Sundar Pichai as displacement activity** — one of FF's most pointed arguments:
- "While I could understand the excitement instigated by the front page of Dainik Bhaskar... the hoopla in the metro-based English language press was surely misplaced." Indians as conformist managers who "refrain from rocking the boat. Clearly a good choice if you are a culturally diverse company like Google" — SOURCE: "InMobi's Miip May Be More Important to India than Pichai" (2015-08-26)

# Founding Fuel: Innovation & R&D — Batch 2 Observations (2015-12-29 to 2017-07-22)

---

## RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES ON INNOVATION

**Innovation requires organizational slack, not TQM-style efficiency**
"TQM helped cut out wastage and made firms a lot more efficient, innovation, on the other hand, actually requires a bit of organisational slack" — SOURCE: "Revving up Innovation" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-12-29)

FF explicitly frames this as a generational leadership problem: CEOs who "ran a tight set of operations in the last 10 years" may not be the right leaders for the next decade, and their boards need to grapple with this. — SOURCE: "Revving up Innovation" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-12-29)

**Innovation metrics are structurally biased against India**
Bloomberg Innovation Index favors R&D-intensive, high-tech manufacturing economies. India's core innovation competencies—affordability, accessibility, inclusivity—are systematically unmeasured. "The driving force for innovation in India is improving accessibility and affordability. But, both the WIPO-Insead Global Innovation Index and Bloomberg don't capture these dimensions well." — SOURCE: "Tracking the progress of innovation in India" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-02-22)

**China is the most serious innovation comparison for India**
FF returns repeatedly to China as the comparative benchmark—not just for manufacturing but for the quality of private entrepreneurship, R&D investment, and innovation culture. "R&D spending in India has never crossed 1% of GDP, and is generally around 0.8-0.9%... At $162 billion, [China's spend] is around 2% of GDP." — SOURCE: "The Chinese innovation machine" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-05-25)

**Funding is not innovation; mega-funding actively destroys it**
"Mega-funding killed the innovation and hunger, the leanness and the sharpness. It created sprawling teams without focus." — SOURCE: "How India's digital economy can rediscover its mojo" by Haresh Chawla (2016-08-30)

**Constraints accelerate innovation, not hinder it**
FF returns to this idea across multiple articles: Carlos Ghosn's frugal engineering, jugaad, Hemingway's six-word story, MINISO's brick-and-mortar model built *around* e-commerce constraints. "Another truism... states that the presence of constraints, as opposed to complete freedom, often better stimulates creativity." — SOURCE: "How variety store MINISO became a mega-success" by CKGSB Knowledge (2017-07-22)

**Grand Challenges and prize-based innovation are underused**
FF promotes X Prize-style mechanisms repeatedly—Kennedy's moon mission, Ansari X Prize, Team Indus, Grand Challenges India. "The idea of stimulating innovation by setting a goal has been adopted by various organizations through prizes for 'grand challenges'." — SOURCE: "Design radical breakthroughs through grand challenges" by Kiran Karnik (2017-01-16)

**Design thinking is powerful but tactically limited without strategic framing**
FF is distinctively critical of design thinking deployed without strategic intent. "There is an inherent danger in the design thinking methodology that renders it tactical rather than strategic." — SOURCE: "What we need to make design thinking strategic" by Baba Prasad (2016-05-15)

**Data must be everyone's business, but "little data" beats big data for most organizations**
Across a five-part series, Nitin Srivastava argues incremental, manually managed data insights outperform expensive analytics infrastructure for resource-constrained firms. "Little Data has a very small effort and capability threshold to cross." — SOURCE: "Creating value with Little Data" by Nitin Srivastava (2016-05-01)

---

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE — WHAT IS DISTINCTIVE

**India's innovation imperative is defined by scale and deprivation, not desire**
"In a country with the largest number of poor and under-nourished people on the planet, what kind of innovation matters, and how should we measure it?" — SOURCE: "Tracking the progress of innovation in India" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-02-22)

**India's structural handicaps are specific and recurring**
- No semiconductor ecosystem: "India missed the semiconductor revolution. We import almost all the modern electronic gadgets we use." — SOURCE: "Transformers: The DNA of an innovative company" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-01-14)
- Absence of risk capital for hardware: Simputer's failure attributed partly to "paucity of risk funding for entrepreneurs, and absence of sophisticated hardware manufacturing in India." — SOURCE: "What lessons does the Simputer hold for Make in India?" by N Dayasindhu (2017-01-13)
- Weak domestic VC for deep tech vs. app-layer investing: "Startups seeking funding from venture capitalists find that it is easier to explain a business in terms of 'We are an Indian version of ABCD' rather than to come up with something that is genuinely original." — SOURCE: "The importance of being Team Indus" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-03-25)

**India's infrastructure stack must be built, not assumed**
"In India you can't take these pieces for granted, and in order to ensure a seamless customer experience—whether it's healthcare, small business loans, or delivering vegetables—you largely have to build the stack and its component parts yourself." — SOURCE: "With patient capital to fix basic problems, India too can think big" by Tom Hyland (2016-05-11)

**India has 800 languages; the entire backbone of the internet is built in English**
Cited as a specific structural barrier to digital inclusion that Western tech discourse ignores entirely. — SOURCE: "With patient capital to fix basic problems, India too can think big" by Tom Hyland (2016-05-11)

**"Reverse innovation" or "innovating for the 6 billion" is India's real opportunity**
GE's MAC 400 ECG machine is the paradigmatic case: designed in India for Indian conditions (fluctuating power, dust, humidity), at one-hundredth the cost of existing machines, then exported globally. "R&D in developed countries will focus on 1 billion of the world's population while R&D in countries like India should focus on the rest of the 6 billion." — SOURCE: "Innovating for a 6 billion-strong market" by N Dayasindhu (2017-01-27)

**Aadhaar / IndiaStack as a unique innovation platform**
FF frames Aadhaar not merely as a welfare program but as a platform for unprecedented innovation—the fastest digital platform to reach a billion users. "The value comes from people and organizations using the Aadhar system to bring down the cost of service delivery dramatically." — SOURCE: "Aadhaar: A quiet disruption" by N S Ramnath (2016-06-25)

India's household debt to GDP at 9% (vs. China's 38%), with majority of consumer debt from informal sources—IndiaStack as the mechanism to formalize this. — SOURCE: "India's silent march and a couple of big ideas in impact investing" by Sahil Kini (2017-05-31)

**India's healthcare crisis as innovation laboratory**
Infant mortality worse than Bangladesh and Nepal at comparable spending; only 150,000 of 1 million new cancer patients get treatment; but Aravind Eye Care, Narayana Health, Jaipur Foot demonstrate that India can pioneer globally replicable low-cost healthcare models. — SOURCE: "Affordable healthcare: India's big opportunity" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2017-03-10); "The state of cancer research and the future of innovation" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-03-08)

**Jugaad as embedded Indian innovation DNA**
"Frugal engineering and disruptive innovation are embedded in our psyche. We have always called it jugaad... by our very nature, we are built to make do with less." — SOURCE: "Moderate constraints actually boost creativity. Here's why" by Charles Assisi (2017-04-22)

**Make in India is insufficient; "Think in India" is the aspiration**
Kiran Karnik explicitly argues Make in India is a "dated idea"—the focus should be on Think in India. — SOURCE: "The growth mindset" by Founding Fuel (2017-03-12)

---

## FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, MENTAL MODELS APPEARING REPEATEDLY

**Design Thinking**
Referenced in nearly every second article: IDEO, Jeanne Liedtka (Darden), CKGSB Knowledge series, Amrita Chowdhury on Swachh Bharat, Indrajit Gupta on enterprise learning. The OODA loop is introduced as a strategic counterweight to design thinking's tactical bias. — SOURCE: "What we need to make design thinking strategic" by Baba Prasad (2016-05-15)

**Clayton Christensen — Disruptive Innovation / Jobs to Be Done**
Cited in multiple articles. Kiran Karnik lists *The Innovator's Dilemma* as must-read. FF runs a full CKGSB Knowledge interview on *Competing Against Luck*. "Innovation doesn't have to be a game of chance if you truly understand how people make the decision to purchase one product or service." — SOURCE: "Clayton Christensen on innovation: Finding the jobs to be done" by CKGSB Knowledge (2017-05-09)

**Gerd Gigerenzer — Heuristics and Ecological Rationality**
Positioned as a counterweight to big data optimism: simple rules of thumb outperform complex models under genuine uncertainty (as opposed to calculable risk). "When you are dealing with uncertainty, [complex models] don't work well, because the world is dynamic. What you then need is a set of simple rules of thumb that are robust." — SOURCE: "Gigerenzer's simple rules" by N S Ramnath (2017-02-19)

**X Prize / Grand Challenge model**
Orteig Prize, Ansari X Prize, Longitude Prize, Team Indus—recurring mechanism for incentivizing breakthrough innovation. — SOURCE: "Design radical breakthroughs through grand challenges" by Kiran Karnik (2017-01-16); "The importance of being Team Indus" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-03-25)

**John Boyd's OODA Loop**
Introduced as a strategic frame that supersedes design thinking's iterative loop—faster cycle time confers competitive advantage independent of the quality of individual innovations. — SOURCE: "What we need to make design thinking strategic" by Baba Prasad (2016-05-15)

**Tony Seba's "zero to one" business model innovation frame**
Applied specifically to solar energy: SunEdison's "zero money down" PPA model as a business model innovation, not a technology innovation, that triggered adoption. — SOURCE: "Policymakers should get out of the way of solar: Tony Seba" by Founding Fuel (2016-11-14)

**Robert Gordon's productivity research**
Used to frame AI skepticism: the third industrial revolution (computers, internet) underperformed the first two in total factor productivity gains. "Growth in total factor productivity was much faster between 1920 and 1970 than either before 1920 or since 1970." — SOURCE: "This week in disruptive tech—February 3, 2016" by N S Ramnath (2016-02-03)

**Kathleen Eisenhardt's hypercompetition theory**
Cited to explain Chinese innovation: in hypercompetitive environments, advantages are not enduring; reinvention is the only sustainable capability. — SOURCE: "The Chinese way" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-04-14)

**Theory of Constraints (Goldratt)**
Linked to jugaad and frugal engineering as embedded Indian innovation orientation. — SOURCE: "Moderate constraints actually boost creativity. Here's why" by Charles Assisi (2017-04-22)

**Holacracy**
Featured as an alternative organizational OS—replacing manager hierarchy with embedded group processes. FF neither endorses nor attacks, but presents as evidence of the structural tension between innovation and hierarchy. — SOURCE: "Holacracy, managerless offices and the future of work" by CKGSB Knowledge (2016-03-08)

---

## WHAT FF IS SKEPTICAL OF / PUSHES BACK AGAINST

**Startup hype and vanity metrics**
"Many startups are centred around apps, offering convenience as their value proposition." "I really wonder how many food delivery companies we need." — SOURCE: "The importance of being Team Indus" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-03-25)

"Funding became the distraction." FF is explicit that India's startup ecosystem celebrated fundraising as success rather than building sustainable businesses. — SOURCE: "How India's digital economy can rediscover its mojo" by Haresh Chawla (2016-08-30)

**India as China-copycat in innovation discourse**
FF resists both the dismissal of Chinese innovation ("China as copycat") and uncritical celebration of India's startup credentials. — SOURCE: "The Chinese way" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-04-14); "The Chinese innovation machine" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-05-25)

**Make in India as innovation policy**
"Make in India is a dated idea." Regulatory-driven innovation (BS-VI norms) is acknowledged as real but insufficient. — SOURCE: "The growth mindset" by Founding Fuel (2017-03-12)

**Personalized medicine / targeted cancer therapies**
"At this point of time, personalised and targeted medicines seem to be more hype than reality." Jan Vijg cited as arguing the age of major technological progress is over. — SOURCE: "The state of cancer research and the future of innovation" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-03-08)

**Silicon Valley techno-optimism applied uncritically to India**
"We know that the Indian government spends less 1% of the GDP on healthcare. How can AI solve the problem that we have less than one hospital bed for a 1,000 Indians?" — SOURCE: "With patient capital to fix basic problems, India too can think big" by Tom Hyland (2016-05-11)

**Product innovation divorced from pricing strategy**
Georg Tacke's critique: 72-76% of new products fail because companies "build it and try to sell it" rather than "design the product around the price." Amazon Fire Phone as canonical failure case. — SOURCE: "Innovation the smart way, an interview with Georg Tacke" by CKGSB Knowledge (2017-04-07)

**Correlation-based data science as innovation driver**
FF explicitly contrasts Christensen's "jobs to be done" with spurious correlations (Tyler Vigen's work cited). "If you are a specific type of customer, you will buy a certain type of product, because there is a correlation between the two" is the view FF argues against. — SOURCE: "Innovation: Starting with the real jobs that need to be done" by Founding Fuel (2017-05-14)

**Big Data over Little Data for resource-constrained organizations**
"Big Data, with its mighty investments and equally spectacular returns" is explicitly positioned as the wrong frame for most Indian companies and startups. — SOURCE: "Three Little Data hacks that keep your costs minimal" by Nitin Srivastava (2016-06-19)

**Steve Jobs as design thinking exemplar**
Jeanne Liedtka explicitly: "I think it's hard to argue that somebody like Steve Jobs actually used design thinking. I mean, he was a creative genius. He came up with an idea in his own head... That's not design thinking." — SOURCE: "Design and business: Jeanne Liedtka on how to think like a designer" by CKGSB Knowledge (2016-06-20)

# Dense Observations: Innovation & R&D — Founding Fuel Batch 3 (2017-2020)

---

## RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES ON INNOVATION

**India as the world's premier laboratory for frugal/social innovation**
- "India is the biggest laboratory of social innovation in the world" — SOURCE: "How to innovate for India" by Indrajit Gupta (2017-12-30)
- "Frugal innovation isn't about doing more with less resources, but about doing better with less. And this is where India has a fantastic opportunity to write the next playbook for innovation, which even the West will adopt." — SOURCE: "The alchemy that transforms adversity into opportunity" by Founding Fuel (2018-01-05)
- India's "cultural advantage is frugality and sustainability" (Dr. Gopichand Katragadda) — SOURCE: "The alchemy that transforms adversity into opportunity" by Founding Fuel (2018-01-05)

**Corporations must partner with startups; neither can innovate alone**

## RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES ON THIS THEME

**Systems redesign vs. incremental fitting**
The solar ferry Aditya story makes explicit that "for new technology to work, often, you will have to redesign an entire system" rather than retrofit old infrastructure. Sandith Thandasherry didn't add solar panels to a wooden ferry; he redesigned from scratch using fibre-reinforced plastic and aluminium, cutting weight from 35 to 17 tonnes. — SOURCE: "Sandith Thandasherry and what it takes to run a boat on solar power" by N S Ramnath (2020-07-29)

**Innovation requires knowing when to violate principles, not just follow them**
Kasparov's line: "To become good at anything you have to know how to apply basic principles. To become great at it, you have to know when to violate those principles." FF treats this as the dividing line between competence and genuine innovation. — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #149: From good to great in the age of AI" by Founding Fuel (2020-08-19)

**The scientific method beats intuition in entrepreneurship**
Repeated citation of the Italian startup study (116 firms, randomised trial) showing that entrepreneurs who followed the scientific method—framing, hypothesis, testing, metrics—got more customers, higher revenues, and were more willing to pivot or shut down. — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #94: Are you measuring what matters?" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-25)

**Platforms vs. apps: fundamentally different problems**
"Building infrastructure is an engineering problem, whereas building an app is a marketing problem." FF argues Jio's scale won't automatically translate into app success; the network effect, not user base, is what matters. "Jio's own earlier efforts to create a WhatsApp competitor wasn't successful." — SOURCE: "Can Jio scale its apps; from rough sketch to photo-real; automation's limits" by N S Ramnath (2020-06-10)

**Creativity and procrastination are linked, not opposed**
Repeated reference to Adam Grant, Leonardo da Vinci (16 years on Mona Lisa), MLK's last-minute "I have a dream" improvisation, Isaacson on da Vinci's intentional marination of ideas. "By delaying the task of finalizing the speech until the very last minute, he left himself open to the widest range of possible ideas." This is treated as a design principle, not a personality quirk. — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #115: Adam Grant on creative people (and procrastination)" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-16); "FF Daily #337: Creativity requires time for ideas to marinate" by Founding Fuel (2021-04-03)

**Disruption is a specific three-phase process, not mere change**
Broughton's framework: Phase 1 (new market, lower end), Phase 2 (technology improvement enables upmarket move), Phase 3 (cardiologists taking cardiac surgeons' patients). FF explicitly criticises the loose use of the word: "a new kind of coffee shop...That is not disruption." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #453: The phases of disruption" by Founding Fuel (2021-08-21)

**Frictions, not insufficient fuel, kill innovations**
Nordgren and Schonthal's argument: "By focusing on Fuel to enhance attraction, innovators neglect the other half of the equation—the Friction that works against the change we seek to create." FF endorses this as a "contrarian" corrective to conventional innovation thinking. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #382: The battle between fuel and friction" by Founding Fuel (2021-05-29)

**Outsiders crack problems insiders can't**
The InnoCentive/Exxon Valdez example: John Davis, a chemist, solved the chocolate mousse problem using a concrete vibrator analogy. Epstein's explanation: insiders are trapped by accumulated industry knowledge. "We tend to view things with all the information we've gathered in our industry, and sometimes that puts us down a path that goes into a wall." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #446: Why outsiders may be better at problem-solving" by Founding Fuel (2021-08-12)

**Collaboration is the engine of modern science, not the lone genius**
India's LIGO paper had over 1,000 authors. The average number of authors per paper rose from 3.2 to 4.4 between 1996–2015. Bhatnagar's collaboration with Steel Brothers & Co. as an origin story for Indian industrial R&D. — SOURCE: "For ease of doing science, India must foster ease of collaborations" by N Dayasindhu (2021-03-17)

**GDP is a broken metric for measuring progress**
Smil's argument amplified: GDP rises when people go to jail, when forests are illegally logged, when drunk-driving accidents increase. "We 'know better, but we still worship high annual GDP growth rate, regardless of where it comes from.'" FF explicitly endorses this critique as applying to India's innovation discourse too. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #416: Practical innovation" by Founding Fuel (2021-07-06)

## INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**Indian firms learning to innovate independently after joint ventures dissolve**
The Hero-Honda, Bajaj-Kawasaki, TVS-Suzuki cases: Indian OEMs account for 77% of the world's largest motorcycle market after separating from Japanese partners. Hero MotoCorp has ~65% share in sub-125cc segment. But the authors ask a harder question: "Is the Indian motorcycle industry the ideal role model for the renaissance of Indian industry, particularly in manufacturing?"—and subject the thesis to scrutiny rather than celebrating uncritically. — SOURCE: "Indian motorcycle industry: A role model for Atmanirbhar Bharat?" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2020-08-13)

**India's R&D collaboration deficit**
India's share of papers from industry-university collaboration declined at -6.1% CAGR (2009–2013) vs. global -3.7%. China grew at +1.3% CAGR in the same period. FF argues this is the structural problem behind India's inability to translate scientific talent into industrial innovation. — SOURCE: "For ease of doing science, India must foster ease of collaborations" by N Dayasindhu (2021-03-17)

**The "missed call" as India-specific innovation**
ZipDial: "A consumer hack that, in the 2000s, before India's cheap smartphone and data revolution, grew more popular than texting." FF treats this as an example of constraint-driven bottom-up innovation unique to India's cost structure. "In 2008, one study estimated that more than half of Indian phone users were in the habit of calling people with the expectation that they wouldn't pick up." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #349: A history of missed calls" by Founding Fuel (2021-04-17)

**Local knowledge as irreplaceable innovation input**
Harish Hande: "If I look at the collapse of our industry in the rural areas, rural businesses, none of them had the capability to help them, because they did not know what the ecosystem was like." IIM/IIT graduates described as "the most useless characters for advice" in rural contexts. FF uses this to argue against elite-institution-centric innovation models. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #311: What's common to Leonardo da Vinci, Steve Jobs & Albert Einstein" by Founding Fuel (2021-03-03)

**Bottom-up, shopfloor-level innovation**
The Nokia Chennai factory story: an assembly-line worker devised a weight-based quality check that was eventually adopted globally. The roller-skate solution for Coimbatore textile workers. These are treated as exemplars of what FF calls innovation "by people closest to the problem." — SOURCE: "What to copy from China" by N S Ramnath (2020-07-04)

**India's quantum ambition as policy bet**
"India just announced the budget for quantum." Compared to China, EU, Canada. Described as "one of the few countries which has an AI policy at the government level." FF frames this as potentially significant but early-stage. — SOURCE: "Building a career in frontier science" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-01)

**India's genomics opportunity tied to database building**
Mapmygenome's Genomepatri: building India's genomic database while monetising consumer health tests. "This wealth of genetic information contains clues about (and potentially cures for) some of the most pervasive diseases which afflict our population." — SOURCE: "Is it in the genes?" by Founding Fuel (2021-06-26)

**India's agritech trust deficit as innovation opportunity**
"A lot of Indian agriculture's problem is on account of the trust deficit, and most of it occurs during the trade of farm produce. There are no objective quality standards nor any means of rapid and reliable testing." AgNext's point-of-transaction testing as addressing this specifically. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #283: Technology and trust in agriculture" by Founding Fuel (2021-01-28)

**India's Raychaudhuri equation as uncelebrated foundation for Nobel-winning physics**
Amalkumar Raychaudhuri's 1955 formulation as the mathematical basis for Penrose's singularity theorems. "Without Raychaudhuri's formalism, and Hawking's early work connecting it to black holes, this work of Penrose may have not happened at all." Used to argue India has deep scientific contributions that go unrecognised. — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #199: Roger Penrose's India connect" by Founding Fuel (2020-10-08)

**TIFR origin story: institution-building as prerequisite for science**
Bhabha's realization that "scientific institutions in India were small, badly run, and short of funds and ideas" and that he needed to build a model institution before the science could happen. The Tata philanthropic network as enabling condition. — SOURCE: "The birth of a model scientific institute" by Hari Pulakkat (2021-05-15)

**IIT culture creates "fixed mindset" conditioning**
Parul Gupta (Springboard co-founder, IIT-B alumna): "In India, how we grow up, an almost 'fixed mindset' is beaten down in our heads. It was only when I started my entrepreneurial journey that I really pushed my boundaries... It was unlearning of everything I had lived my life by." — SOURCE: "An edtech entrepreneur's learning journey" by Founding Fuel (2021-11-11)

- Related: "Never fall in love with your own idea." — SOURCE: "FF Insights 681: The Moses trap" by Founding Fuel (2022-08-30)

**Experiment continuously; treat early work as experiments, not commitments**
- Lean startup methodology: "In the early days, treat everything as an experiment. Failure is upsetting to so many of us because it implies finality... an experiment, which you recognise from the beginning has an uncertain outcome, can hardly be called a failure." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #696: Treat everything as an experiment" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-07)
- Bezos: "Outsized returns often come from betting against conventional wisdom... Given a ten percent chance of a 100 times payoff, you should take that bet every time. But you're still going to be wrong nine times out of ten." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #697: Betting against conventional wisdom" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-07)
- "Start now, not when it's easier down the road. Great products take time to develop—you can't buy them later when resources aren't as tight." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #597: Playing it safe won't save you" by Founding Fuel (2022-02-26)

**Ideas and businesses evolve — disruptive framing is retrospective, not predictive**
- Safi Bahcall: "Early-stage projects in rapidly evolving markets behave like a leaf in a tornado... It's easy to point to technologies that disrupted a market in hindsight, once the leaf has landed." Google's PageRank was a "sustaining" innovation; Sam Walton ended up in Bentonville partly for quail hunting. — SOURCE: "FF Insights #592: Sustainable innovation" by Founding Fuel (2022-02-19)

**Metrics are the enemy of creativity and genuine innovation**
- "The calculative... is the enemy of the imaginative." Metrics "inhibit risk-taking, an inevitable concomitant of exploration and creativity." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #684: The enemy of creativity" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-07)
- Roger Martin: "You can't chart a course for the future or bring about change merely by analysing history. Customer behaviour will never be transformed by a product whose design is based on an analysis of past behaviour." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #684: The enemy of creativity" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-07)

**Learning organisations iterate continuously (do-learn-do)**
- PE firms as "learning organisations" that "develop successful formulas that they (1) can repeat within a business and (2) can replicate outside the business." Nike's repeatable formula across sports categories. — SOURCE: "FF Insights #600: Learning organisations" by Founding Fuel (2022-03-02)
- Andreessen's rule as a VC: "favouring startups whose founders focused on running code and customer service rather than charts and presentations. 'The former are the ones who become the trillion-dollar companies.'" — SOURCE: "FF Insights #701: Making trillion-dollar companies" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-08)

**AI's fundamental limitations are being voiced by its own architects**
- LeCun: "There's absolutely no way that autoregressive LLMs... will reach human intelligence." Today's LLMs will be "largely obsolete within five years." — SOURCE: "Are LLMs Just Clever Parrots?" by Shishir Prasad (2025-10-27)
- Sutton: "LLMs are mimetic machines—they imitate rather than act." Karpathy: "They don't have continual learning... They're cognitively lacking." — SOURCE: "Are LLMs Just Clever Parrots?" by Shishir Prasad (2025-10-27)
- The godfathers are "either stepping away from LLMs or deliberately staying away from them." — SOURCE: "Revolution Inside AI" by Sundeep Waslekar (2025-12-21)

## II. FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**India's missed hardware/semiconductor opportunity — a recurring historical wound**
- "Indians even today bemoan the fact that while we are globally renowned for software and allied services, we have not made any meaningful contribution in hardware manufacturing." CDC's 1965 proposal for a core-memory manufacturing venture in India "went into cold storage." "Did we miss an opportunity in the 1960s?" Bhabha's death in 1966 is identified as a turning point. — SOURCE: "When India made its first computer" by Founding Fuel (2022-11-18)

**Zoho as the counter-model to mainstream Indian tech**
- "You don't hear much about Zoho because it is bootstrapped and not funded by VC money." Zoho serves 50 million employees — comparable to TCS+Infosys+Cognizant+Wipro's combined client base. "Sridhar Vembu is an archetype of the generation of CEOs that India needs." — SOURCE: "Building Back Better: Lessons from Zoho's founder" by Founding Fuel (2022-06-20)
- Vembu's critique of the Indian software sector's myopia: "The idea of core competence should be challenged. It has kept, for example, the software industry in India from investing in semiconductors or cloud infrastructure." — SOURCE: "Building Back Better: Lessons from Zoho's founder" by Founding Fuel (2022-06-20)
- Vembu on GE's Jack Welch as "false idol": financialisation over engineering R&D. "India is tempted to follow—not invest in R&D, manufacturing prowess, and basic capabilities, and instead go for cheap finance. India should be careful not to copy this approach." — SOURCE: "Building Back Better: Lessons from Zoho's founder" by Founding Fuel (2022-06-20)

**India as a bazaar, not a cathedral — innovation through improvisation at scale**
- "We are, quite literally, a bazaar... a farmer using voice AI to check mandi rates in Marathi. A homemaker using image-to-text tools to help her child with schoolwork... India's strength lies in stretching technologies to local needs, reshaping them, and unlocking business models rooted in context." — SOURCE: "From Bazaar to Breakthrough" by Shrinath V (2025-06-18)
- The mobile telephony arc: CRBTs as "a rare space for digital self-expression" for first-time mobile users; a Tamil song as a caller tone builds trust with patients from Tamil Nadu. "Use cases are not always discovered by companies designing products or services. They're discovered by users." — SOURCE: "From Bazaar to Breakthrough" by Shrinath V (2025-06-18)

**Nilekani's "billion-user bet" — India's DPI stack as an innovation framework**
- WhatsApp moment analogy applied to UPI; "virtuous cycle" of adoption driven by identity (Aadhaar), network effects, and falling smartphone costs. The 2015 prediction came true. — SOURCE: "The Billion-User Bet" by NS Ramnath (2025-03-27)
- DeepSeek's launch "deflated some of the swagger even among the tech community, which prided itself on frugal innovation." — SOURCE: "The Billion-User Bet" by NS Ramnath (2025-03-27)

**India's food security R&D: CRISPR, gene guns, and climate change**
- Mahyco/Barwale: India avoided famine through Green Revolution hybrids, but "climate change is beginning to undo that progress." National farm output could fall 15-18% this century. Usha Zehr now deploying CRISPR, "gene guns," and bacteria-based gene insertion. "The only reason I'm optimistic is because technology is available." — SOURCE: "The race for food security" by Founding Fuel (2022-04-09)

**Pusa decomposer: fungi solving Delhi's air pollution**
- Indian Agricultural Research Institute's cocktail of seven naturally occurring fungi decomposes crop stubble instead of burning it, reduces chemical fertilizer dependence by 25%. "300g of the formula is enough to spray on roughly half a hectare." An example of jugaad-meets-science. — SOURCE: "FF Insights #627: A chance to be something specific" by Founding Fuel (2022-04-09)

**Navigation/mapping in India — adoption requires familiar anchors**
- "The fiercest competition for new technology is rarely another product. It's the habit people already trust." India wasn't ready to trade a human guide for a digital one in 2007. The same navigation product needed three different pitches for Delhi, Mumbai, and Bangalore. — SOURCE: "Maps, History, and Finding the Throughline" by Shrinath V (2025-07-25)

**Digital therapeutics and personalised medicine emerging in India**
- QuitSure app "app-ifying" counseling-centre treatment protocols. Digital therapeutics as a domain that "holds much potential, and is finding many takers." — SOURCE: "FF Life: Personalised medicine and healthcare" by Charles Assisi (2023-01-21)

**The AI divide within India**
- "AI on Wheels" — Sachin Joshi's bus loaded with tech tools going to slums of Nashik, educating children of casual labourers. "Many 10-year-old children do not have the ability to read and write that five- or six-year-old children at the beginning of primary school are supposed to have." — SOURCE: "At the top and bottom of the AI debate" by Sundeep Waslekar (2025-02-22)

**Raghuram Rajan/Rohit Lamba's thesis: India must focus on services and tech-led industries**
- "India should focus on manufacturing services and tech-led, read coding-led, industries." Warning: "we must not assume that low-cost assembly will lead to higher value-added manufacturing." India's advantage is English-medium education and human capital. — SOURCE: "Eight best business books of 2023" by D Shivakumar (2023-12-15)

## III. FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, AND MENTAL MODELS

**Nomological networks of cumulative evidence (Gad Saad / Darwin)**
- Truth-finding requires replication, literature reviews, meta-analysis, AND "building a network of cumulative evidence stemming from widely different sources." Darwin as exemplar: "amassed a mountain of evidence prior to bringing his case." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #625: The pattern of truth" by Founding Fuel (2022-04-09)

**The extended mind theory (Andy Clark and David Chalmers)**
- "Cognitive processes are not confined to the brain. They can extend into the external world through tools and technologies... If a tool reliably aids in our memory or problem-solving skills, it should be considered part of the mind." Applied to AI notetakers. — SOURCE: "Our extended minds and AI notetakers" by NS Ramnath (2025-05-16)

**Cathedral vs. Bazaar (Eric S. Raymond)**
- Applied to India's technology adoption: "The 'cathedral' is deliberate, top-down, and orderly... The 'bazaar', by contrast, is open, noisy, and constantly evolving. It thrives on contribution, improvisation, and emergence." — SOURCE: "From Bazaar to Breakthrough" by Shrinath V (2025-06-18)

**Diffusion of Innovations (Everett Rogers)**
- Applied to AI adoption: innovators, early adopters, majority, laggards. HudZah as innovator. — SOURCE: "AI natives are here. Are you keeping up?" by Kavi Arasu (2025-02-14)

**Digital Natives vs. Digital Immigrants (Marc Prensky, refined by White and Le Cornu)**
- Evolved to "AI natives" and "AI immigrants." "Digital engagement was less about birth year and more about behaviour—some were Visitors, using technology as needed, while others were Residents, living deeply within it." — SOURCE: "AI natives are here. Are you keeping up?" by Kavi Arasu (2025-02-14)

**World models vs. LLMs (LeCun)**
- "A world model is a system that learns the structure of reality—objects, relationships, physical laws, and the consequences of actions—so that it can simulate outcomes before acting... A useful metaphor is a flight simulator rather than a typewriter." — SOURCE: "Revolution Inside AI" by Sundeep Waslekar (2025-12-21)

**Systems thinking as antidote to polarization**
- "We are big fans of systems thinking because we think it's one of the best antidotes to polarisation everywhere." Donella Meadows, Peter Senge's Fifth Discipline, David Peter Stroh. Arun Maira's argument that "modern science is incomplete and even an imprecise tool to understand the world." — SOURCE: "FF Life: Systems thinking — Seeing the whole" by NS Ramnath (2023-09-01)

**Lean startup / test before you invest (Blank, Ries)**
- "Silicon Valley's philosophy of 'test before you invest.'" Treat early work as experiments; Edison's 999 ways not to invent the light bulb. — SOURCE: "FF Insights #696: Treat everything as an experiment" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-07)

**Long-tailed distribution of returns (Bezos)**
- "In business, every once in a while, when you step up to the plate, you can score 1,000 runs. This long-tailed distribution of returns is why it's important to be bold." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #697: Betting against conventional wisdom" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-07)

**First-principles reasoning (Vembu)**
- "I don't accept something as the revealed truth. I like to understand things from first principles, and sometimes a new pathway emerges." — SOURCE: "Building Back Better: Lessons from Zoho's founder" by Founding Fuel (2022-06-20)
